title: Two LISD seniors earn full-ride Terry Scholarships to Texas State and UTSA
excerpt: Briana Gonzalez of Nixon High School and Gabriel Benavides of Martin High School were named 2026 Terry Scholars, earning a full-ride college scholarship for up to eight semesters.
content:
Two Laredo ISD seniors have earned one of the most competitive scholarships in Texas — a full ride to college for up to eight semesters from the Terry Foundation.

Briana Gonzalez of Nixon High School and Gabriel Benavides of Martin High School were named 2026 Terry Scholars, according to Laredo ISD. The scholarship covers their college expenses, and recipients must live on campus their first year in a Terry-designated residence hall and maintain good academic standing to keep the support through their undergraduate years.

Terry Scholars are chosen on three equally weighted criteria: demonstrated leadership and strong character, academic excellence, and financial need.

Gonzalez learned the news in her second-block class, when her phone buzzed with the Terry Foundation interview results. She said she was happy and in shock, and went straight to tell her counselor, Ms. Gonzalez. She said she knew how competitive the scholarship is, and that the sacrifices her parents made to travel to Houston for the interviews made the moment even more meaningful.

She will attend Texas State University in San Marcos, where she plans to major in political science with a minor in criminal justice. She was also selected for the university's President's Leadership cohort — one of 35 chosen from 350 applicants — which will give her a chance to study abroad in her sophomore year, with most expenses covered. She is the first in her family to attend a major university, and after earning her bachelor's degree she wants to attend law school, with hopes of interning with Federal Judge Diana Saldaña and eventually returning to Laredo to work in the legal field.

At Nixon, Gonzalez is a student in the Business, Industry, and Public Services Early College Academy. She served on the Superintendent's Student Advisory Council, Student Council, National Honor Society, Interact Club, Junior Achievement and Spanish Honor Society, and played four years on the girls' soccer team, which won Nixon's first district and bi-district championships this year. She has volunteered with the Laredo Animal Shelter and the St. Augustine Catholic Church youth group. She also credits the Kazen Fellowship Program with confirming her interest in a legal career after shadowing a lawyer and meeting with federal agencies.

Benavides found out while sitting in his EMT class at Laredo College South, getting ready for an exam. He said he was so nervous he asked his best friends to open the email for him — and then called his mother, his number one supporter, right away. He said the scholarship lifts a tremendous financial burden from his family.

Benavides is the salutatorian of the Martin High School Class of 2026 and a student at the Esther G. Buckley Early College Academy. His honors include National Hispanic Scholar and QuestBridge Finalist. He will attend the University of Texas at San Antonio, where he plans to major in civil engineering. He plays euphonium in the Martin band, Banda Del Animo, is a three-year UIL regional qualifier, serves as president of the Library Club, is a member of Health Occupations Students of America, and is part of the Emergency Medical Technician program at Laredo College. In the summer he volunteers with the robotics team at Santa Maria Elementary School.

Sources: Laredo Independent School District, “Laredo ISD students named recipient of Terry Scholarship” (Nov. 2026).
